scope_note: Daily edition from matching Thursday /new listings: 118 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 113 cs.RO rows, 217 deduplicated papers, and 179 ROI papers. Tier A cards are conservative abstract-only autopsies from repository parser output; no figure, table, full-text, code, or dataset-release claim is asserted unless the abstract itself states it.
executive_thesis: The September 17 batch turns robot learning into an evidence-contract problem. VLA papers stop treating the backbone as the only object of study and instead ask which context, layer, action token, future representation, cache, or local fallback has authority to change the robot command. Geometry papers ask when feed-forward 3D, Gaussian splats, LiDAR submaps, sonar-only SLAM, and physical-property maps should be trusted or rejected. Navigation papers turn gaze, grounding, geometric memory, social response, and route constraints into active evidence before committing motion. Contact-rich manipulation papers make force, tactile history, energy, morphology, and generated audio/physics signals explicit correction channels. APRL's opening is to build benchmarks where each representation must prove what decision it changes, when it should be revoked, and what failure evidence would falsify it.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: VLA adaptation is moving to measurable interfaces
decision_cards.body: GPT-Policy, layer-diagnostic LoRA, action tokenizers, FIVE-VLA, RAF-VLA, CSWAM, VLA-ULAP, and rMuscle all expose a specific interface between context, representation, memory, and action.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Geometry models now need trust gates
decision_cards.body: GeoCond, Wind on Trees, CADSplat, NormLift, PhysVGGT, VIO stress tests, SEAM, and SOL-SLAM ask not only whether geometry is reconstructed, but when a robot should believe it.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Execution should be revoked by runtime evidence
decision_cards.body: RoboVAD, OmniRisk, heterogeneous cooperative perception attacks, VLM-MPPI, CALOS, and RiskWorld turn anomaly, risk, adversarial consistency, language mode choice, and safety layers into runtime stop conditions.

papers.title: In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents
papers.fit: robot in-context learning - VLM agent - executable tool actions
papers.status_quo: Robot adaptation is usually treated as fine-tuning or collecting more demonstrations for a fixed policy.
papers.friction: A finite demonstration set cannot cover deployment variation, and VLM reasoning does not automatically become executable robot behavior.
papers.hidden_premise: Context becomes useful only if visual transitions, tool actions, controller verification, and execution feedback remain in one closed loop.
papers.conceptual_move: Use a context compiler, VLM action proposal, constrained controller, and outcome reports as a deployment-time learning loop without gradient updates.
papers.mechanism: The abstract says GPT-Policy preserves task-relevant transitions, proposes robot-tool actions, verifies each action, executes it, and feeds back outcomes.

evidence.claim: Human video demonstrations improve real-robot task completion even without robot action labels.
Aligned action references further help contact-sensitive tasks.
APRL should evaluate which context item changes the next action and which controller check prevents unsafe execution.

papers.falsification: If context examples help only by restating task labels and not by changing verified tool actions, this is prompt retrieval rather than robot learning.
papers.adversarial: Commercial VLM ability can hide brittle low-level control; test unseen object geometry, contact ambiguity, and failed-action feedback.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat in-context learning as a verified action loop, not as a smarter instruction parser.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for tool-mediated manipulation; weaker when actions are continuous and cannot be verified by a constrained controller.

papers.title: ActionPiece: Rethinking Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: action tokenization - physical rank consistency - VLA policy success
papers.status_quo: Action tokenizers are often judged by pointwise reconstruction error such as MSE.
papers.friction: Small pointwise errors can still distort local action adjustments that matter for context-dependent control.
papers.hidden_premise: A token is robot-useful only if it preserves physical relationships among nearby actions after decoding.
papers.conceptual_move: Evaluate and train tokenization with physical rank consistency, supervising near-far order in representation and codeword assignment.
papers.mechanism: The abstract says ActionPiece augments reconstruction with representation and quantization objectives that preserve physical action relationships.

evidence.claim: The paper argues MSE misses diminished, distorted, or reversed context-specific action adjustments.
It reports 94.8 percent on LIBERO and 68.8 percent on unseen LIBERO-Plus under the same Qwen3-VL-4B setup.
APRL should rank action tokenizers by whether recovered actions preserve local intervention order, not only by average error.

papers.falsification: If PRC improves while closed-loop recovery and contact-sensitive success do not, the preserved rank is not the relevant physical relation.
papers.adversarial: Rank consistency may reward smooth action neighborhoods that fail under discontinuous contact events.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask what physical relation the discrete action vocabulary preserves.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for autoregressive VLA policies; less direct for continuous diffusion controllers without discrete action recovery.

papers.title: Not All Layers Need Tuning: Diagnosing and Directing Adaptation in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: VLA adaptation diagnosis - variable-rank LoRA - deployment shifts
papers.status_quo: Parameter-efficient VLA adaptation usually applies similar adapter capacity across model regions.
papers.friction: Appearance, instruction, and novel-object shifts stress different parts of the model, so uniform adaptation wastes capacity or tunes the wrong region.
papers.hidden_premise: A deployment shift has a measurable regional adaptation cost before fine-tuning starts.
papers.conceptual_move: Diagnose per-region cost from a few unlabeled target observations, allocate variable-rank adapters, and freeze calibrated regions.
papers.mechanism: The abstract combines reference-free gradient signals, Monte Carlo Dropout, and CKA against a cached source reference.

evidence.claim: The diagnostic ranks regions at median Spearman 0.91 against isolated fine-tuning costs.
On physical xArm-7 instruction shift, it matches full fine-tuning with 0.04 percent trainable parameters.
APRL should identify whether a failure is vision, language, or action-head adaptation before spending fine-tuning budget.

papers.falsification: If regional rankings change after real contact or long-horizon execution, ten unlabeled observations may underdiagnose the shift.
papers.adversarial: A cached source reference can encode old task biases; stress with object, lighting, instruction, and force shifts simultaneously.
papers.thinking_tool: Measure the adaptation locus before choosing the adapter budget.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for PEFT VLA deployment; less direct when full retraining or modular state estimators dominate adaptation.

papers.title: GeoCond: A Conditioning-Aware Reliability Adapter for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.fit: feed-forward 3D - geometric conditioning - pose uncertainty gate
papers.status_quo: Feed-forward 3D foundation models can output camera, depth, and point maps in one pass, often with native confidence scores.
papers.friction: Low overlap, low parallax, and extreme rotation cause silent failure that native aleatoric confidence may not capture.
papers.hidden_premise: A 3D model should expose geometric conditioning before its pose, depth, or point map is allowed into a robot pipeline.
papers.conceptual_move: Attach a lightweight adapter that reads predicted geometry and outputs pose-level uncertainty plus a refinement gate.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes supervision from permutation orbit variance, ground-truth pose error, or cycle residuals from unlabelled pose graphs.

evidence.claim: GeoCond improves OOD AUSE on VGGT from 0.32 to 0.20 over native confidence.
It avoids collapse caused by applying bundle adjustment uniformly.
APRL should gate map updates by geometric conditioning rather than trusting single-pass 3D uniformly.

papers.falsification: If pose-level uncertainty does not predict downstream navigation or manipulation failure, it is calibration without operational value.
papers.adversarial: Cycle residuals can miss symmetric scenes; test repeated corridors, textureless surfaces, and dynamic objects.
papers.thinking_tool: A feed-forward 3D prediction needs a trust gate before it becomes robot state.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VGGT-like 3D backbones; less direct for SLAM systems with explicit multi-frame optimization.

papers.title: Wind on Trees: Testing Physical Grounding in Dynamic 4D Gaussian Splatting
papers.fit: dynamic 4DGS - physical prior - extrapolation and parameter recovery
papers.status_quo: Dynamic 4DGS can optimize photometric consistency and appear physically plausible.
papers.friction: Wind-driven vegetation is underconstrained, so the optimized deformation can fit views without recovering the true motion process.
papers.hidden_premise: Physical grounding should be tested by extrapolation, unseen driving conditions, and recovery of latent physical parameters.
papers.conceptual_move: Replace generic learned deformation with a damped-oscillator prior driven by observed wind, then test held-out views, time, wind speeds, and parameters.
papers.mechanism: The abstract says the prior improves extrapolation but parameter recovery is weak, with damping not recovered at all.

evidence.claim: The physical prior costs in-distribution appearance fidelity but extrapolates better outside the training window and wind.
Frequency recovery survives a null control only on the sparsest tree, and damping is not recovered.
APRL should separate visual fit, extrapolation, and physical parameter validity in dynamic maps.

papers.falsification: If the same prior fails on real vegetation or robot-mounted observations, the synthetic testbed may isolate only a narrow motion family.
papers.adversarial: A physics prior can be a good regularizer without identifying the real physical variables; use null controls and downstream planning tests.
papers.thinking_tool: Physical grounding is not visual plausibility; it is parameter recovery and valid extrapolation.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for dynamic 3D scene evaluation; less direct for rigid indoor mapping unless dynamics are present.

papers.title: GroundingVLN: Reasoning and Acting with Grounding for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.fit: vision-language navigation - grounded reasoning - pixel goal execution
papers.status_quo: VLN agents often reason semantically but hand a vague high-level decision to low-level motion.
papers.friction: Intermediate reasoning can be unanchored from visual evidence, and spatial decisions can lack precise goals.
papers.hidden_premise: Grounding can be the shared interface between language reasoning and geometric control.
papers.conceptual_move: Anchor reasoning to task-relevant image locations and predict a progress-aligned pixel goal that a geometric planner can execute.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes GroundingCOTVLN-188K and execution-aware reinforcement learning to align reasoning and spatial decisions.

evidence.claim: GroundingVLN reports 69.9 percent SR on R2R-CE and 75.1 percent SR on RxR-CE.
It uses 0.9 percent as much training data as the strongest baseline according to the abstract.
APRL should evaluate whether a grounded landmark actually changes the next waypoint and reduces detours.

papers.falsification: If pixel goals improve benchmark scores but fail under moving occluders or map ambiguity, grounding is not stable enough for deployment.
papers.adversarial: Grounded traces can become dataset-specific rationales; test unseen building styles and misleading landmarks.
papers.thinking_tool: A navigation reason should name the visual evidence and the spatial goal it authorizes.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLN and object search; less direct for low-level locomotion without image-goal planners.

papers.title: ForceDelta-VLA: Distilling Force-Conditioned ActionCorrections for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.fit: force-conditioned VLA - action correction - contact-rich manipulation
papers.status_quo: Force-aware VLA policies often mix nominal task motion and contact correction into one action prediction.
papers.friction: Demonstrations rarely label what part of the action is task reference and what part is contact-dependent correction.
papers.hidden_premise: Contact-rich execution should separate slower reference actions from faster force-conditioned corrections.
papers.conceptual_move: Distill explicit force-correction targets from paired force-conditioned and force-agnostic teacher predictions.
papers.mechanism: The abstract says the lightweight policy adjusts reference actions using recent force history and robot state between reference-action updates.

evidence.claim: ForceDelta-VLA reports 82.2 percent mean success versus 54.4 percent for ForceVLA across nine contact-rich tasks.
It reduces mean peak contact force over successful trials by about 26 percent on both platforms.
APRL should score contact corrections by force overshoot, slip recovery, and whether nominal motion remains intact.

papers.falsification: If the correction target depends on one teacher's quirks, it may not transfer across hardware or force sensors.
papers.adversarial: Peak force over successful trials can miss failures; include failed attempts, material changes, and delayed force sensing.
papers.thinking_tool: Separate the action that aims at the task from the action that repairs contact.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for contact-rich manipulation; weaker for tasks where proprioceptive or force signals are sparse.

papers.title: RoboVAD: A Large Cross-Domain Evaluation Benchmark for Anomaly Detection in Robotic Arm Manipulation Videos
papers.fit: robot anomaly detection - cross-domain benchmark - recovery trigger
papers.status_quo: Video anomaly detection benchmarks mostly come from surveillance or traffic rather than robot manipulation.
papers.friction: Robot arms can face unseen tasks and unseen anomaly types, but current resources do not isolate that cross-domain failure.
papers.hidden_premise: Recovery systems need anomaly detectors that generalize across both action domains and anomaly families.
papers.conceptual_move: Construct a robotic arm VAD benchmark with held-out tasks and held-out anomaly types, then test adapted VAD methods.
papers.mechanism: The abstract frames anomalies as mistakes during robotic arm tasks and evaluates frame-level detection under cross-domain splits.

evidence.claim: All tested methods remain below 70 percent micro-averaged frame-level AUC in the most challenging setup.
The benchmark is designed for unforeseen tasks and new anomaly types.
APRL should use anomaly detection as a recovery trigger only after cross-task and cross-anomaly validation.

papers.falsification: If anomalies are visually obvious but not control-relevant, the benchmark may not predict real intervention value.
papers.adversarial: Frame AUC can reward late detection; add lead-time, recoverability, and false-stop cost metrics.
papers.thinking_tool: An anomaly benchmark should test whether the recovery trigger sees the failure before it matters.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation video monitoring; less direct for force-only or state-only anomalies.

papers.title: OmniRisk: Omnidirectional Trajectory-Risk Learning for Agile Quadrotor Dynamic Avoidance
papers.fit: quadrotor avoidance - trajectory risk - onboard primitive selection
papers.status_quo: Online trajectory optimization can either scale poorly with obstacle count or stay fast while losing reliability in dense dynamic encounters.
papers.friction: Sparse range observations do not directly reveal obstacle motion, yet agile avoidance needs reaction within short windows.
papers.hidden_premise: Risk should be learned as trajectory-level evidence aligned with obstacle velocity, then reused cheaply at runtime.
papers.conceptual_move: Predict terminal boundary states and dynamic risks over an omnidirectional primitive lattice in one forward pass.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes LiDAR panoramas, dynamic masks, Cartesian surface velocities, and an asymmetric velocity-aligned risk field.

evidence.claim: Risk inference cost is independent of obstacle count because online accumulation is removed.
Real-world flights demonstrate consecutive evasive maneuvers at relative encounter speeds up to 15 m/s without fine-tuning.
APRL should compare risk fields by unnecessary hesitation after obstacles pass, not just collision avoidance.

papers.falsification: If the risk field fails under sensor dropout or adversarial motion, the fixed primitive lattice may be too narrow.
papers.adversarial: Velocity-aligned risk can underweight rare lateral maneuvers; stress with accelerating and occluded obstacles.
papers.thinking_tool: Runtime safety needs a risk field that knows when danger is approaching and when it has passed.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for agile aerial robots; analogous but not direct for ground robots with different dynamics.

papers.title: VLA-ULAP: Interleaving Cloud VLA Calls with Ultra-Lightweight Local Action Prediction at the Edge
papers.fit: edge VLA - local fallback - latency-aware execution
papers.status_quo: Billion-parameter VLA policies often assume onboard compute or remote inference can keep up with control demands.
papers.friction: Power limits and communication delay make remote calls too slow for dynamic robot response.
papers.hidden_premise: A small local predictor can hold temporary action authority between cloud VLA calls if its context and history are sufficient.
papers.conceptual_move: Interleave remote VLA calls with a 7.4M-parameter local action predictor using current views, proprioception, and executed action history.
papers.mechanism: The abstract says ULAP predicts action chunks independently, without VLA hidden states or server round trips.

evidence.claim: ULAP removes 48.8 to 76.7 percent of VLA calls while retaining 95.0 to 97.5 percent baseline success in simulated settings.
Physical SO-101 experiments retain 95.2 to 100 percent baseline success while reducing estimated inference time and device energy.
APRL should evaluate local fallback by latency-aware success, not by average policy agreement alone.

papers.falsification: If local predictors miss rare contact transitions or unexpected objects, call reduction can hide safety debt.
papers.adversarial: Measure false local autonomy: cases where the cloud call would have corrected a trajectory but ULAP continues stale action chunks.
papers.thinking_tool: Edge deployment is an authority handoff between remote intelligence and local muscle memory.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for repetitive or latency-sensitive manipulation; less direct for open-ended tasks requiring new reasoning at each step.

synthesis.title: VLA papers are exposing action authority variables
synthesis.links: GPT-Policy - Not All Layers Need Tuning - M2Tok - ActionPiece - FIVE-VLA - RAF-VLA - CSWAM - VLA-ULAP - rMuscle
synthesis.facts: The papers name context examples, model regions, action vocabularies, future representations, semantic history, remote calls, and activation caches as variables that affect action.
synthesis.inference: APRL should log which variable actually changes the command under each shift, then revoke authority when the variable no longer predicts recovery.

synthesis.title: Geometry is becoming a decision gate
synthesis.links: GeoCond - Wind on Trees - CADSplat - NormLift - PhysVGGT - VIO stress tests - SEAM - SOL-SLAM
synthesis.facts: The batch separates visual quality from conditioning, physical extrapolation, CAD anchoring, semantic reliability, physical property prediction, submap evidence, and sensor degradation.
synthesis.inference: A robot map should report not only state, but whether this state is conditioned well enough to support localization, contact, planning, or update decisions.

synthesis.title: Runtime safety is moving from static score to revocation timing
synthesis.links: RoboVAD - OmniRisk - HetPoison/HetShield - VLM-MPPI - RiskWorld - CALOS
synthesis.facts: The papers detect unseen manipulation anomalies, predict velocity-aligned trajectory risk, validate cooperative features, choose diverse flight behaviors, replace trajectories selectively, and enforce attitude safety.
synthesis.inference: The evaluation target should be how early and how specifically a system stops, defers, switches mode, or repairs the current plan.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: September 16 framed robot intelligence as authority allocation across world-action, map, contact, safety, and deployment representations.
frontier_memory.body: September 17 strengthens that thesis with more explicit contracts: action tokens preserve physical rank, layers reveal adaptation cost, 3D models expose conditioning, and edge VLAs hand authority to local predictors.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent editions emphasized WAM/VLA evidence but less often the discrete vocabulary of action itself.
frontier_memory.body: M2Tok and ActionPiece make the action tokenizer a central scientific object: the question is whether a token vocabulary preserves controllable physical relations.

frontier_memory.label: Commoditizing
frontier_memory.history: 3DGS, VGGT-style feed-forward 3D, and VLA deployment papers have appeared repeatedly across September.
frontier_memory.body: The differentiator is now the trust or revocation gate around these systems, not the fact of using Gaussian splats, geometry foundation models, or large VLA backbones.

frontier_memory.label: Contradiction
frontier_memory.history: Bigger context and richer world models are often assumed to help embodiment.
frontier_memory.body: Today complicates that: Wind on Trees improves extrapolation while failing parameter recovery, VLA-ULAP removes many cloud VLA calls, and layer diagnostics suggest most regions need not be tuned.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: The repo has separate lines for action-interface audits, geometry trust, runtime safety, and contact correction.
frontier_memory.body: A shared evidence-contract benchmark is still missing: one suite should ask when context, geometry, force, risk, and local fallback are allowed to change a robot decision.

strategy.title: Robot evidence-contract benchmark
strategy.thesis: Build one benchmark where context, action tokens, geometry, force, risk, and edge fallback must each declare the decision they can change and the revocation condition.
strategy.one_week: Prototype three tasks: action-token rank preservation on LIBERO, GeoCond-style map trust on sparse-view scenes, and ForceDelta-style correction on one contact task.
strategy.four_week: Unify action deltas, geometric trust gates, force corrections, anomaly lead time, and local/cloud handoff logs under one evidence-contract schema.
strategy.success: At least two evidence variables predict failure or recovery earlier than terminal success and change intervention timing.
strategy.stop: Stop if all variables reduce to generic confidence and do not alter action, map update, contact correction, or defer behavior.
strategy.paper_path: A benchmark and analysis paper on representation authority and revocation in robot execution.
strategy.asset_path: Authority-labeled episodes, action-token rankings, geometry conditioning labels, force correction traces, anomaly lead-time labels, and edge fallback decisions.
strategy.asset: Authority-labeled episodes, action-token rankings, geometry conditioning labels, force correction traces, anomaly lead-time labels, and edge fallback decisions.

strategy.title: Geometry trust gate for robot maps
strategy.thesis: Turn feed-forward 3D, 3DGS, LiDAR, sonar, and physical-property outputs into map-update and planning gates instead of passive perception products.
strategy.one_week: Stress one reconstruction stack with low overlap, low parallax, dynamic object insertion, and sensor degradation, then score pose uncertainty versus downstream failure.
strategy.four_week: Compare GeoCond-style conditioning, NormLift semantic reliability, SEAM submap evidence, VIO perturbation thresholds, and sonar-only local SLAM gates.
strategy.success: Trust gates predict harmful localization, map-update, or grasp-planning errors before the downstream task fails.
strategy.stop: Stop if gates improve calibration curves but do not change robot decisions or recovery outcomes.
strategy.paper_path: A robot-usable geometry evaluation paper centered on trust gating rather than visual fidelity.
strategy.asset_path: Sparse-view scenes, degradation scripts, submap-change labels, sonar/LiDAR sequences, conditioning scores, and decision outcomes.
strategy.asset: Sparse-view scenes, degradation scripts, submap-change labels, sonar/LiDAR sequences, conditioning scores, and decision outcomes.

strategy.title: Contact-correction authority stack
strategy.thesis: Separate nominal task motion from force, tactile, energy, morphology, and generated audio/physics correction channels for contact-rich manipulation.
strategy.one_week: Run one contact task with force-conditioned correction, tactile prior, and energy regularization ablations; measure peak force, slip, and recovery timing.
strategy.four_week: Add cross-embodiment grasp geometry, deformable asset generation, and audio-shaped desired-force profiles into one correction benchmark.
strategy.success: Correction channels predict when nominal action should be overridden and reduce force overshoot or invalid contact on unseen objects.
strategy.stop: Stop if contact channels raise average success but cannot explain or anticipate failure modes.
strategy.paper_path: A contact-rich manipulation paper on explicit correction authority across sensing and embodiment channels.
strategy.asset_path: Force histories, tactile/proprioceptive traces, contact labels, embodiment tokens, generated deformable assets, and recovery annotations.
strategy.asset: Force histories, tactile/proprioceptive traces, contact labels, embodiment tokens, generated deformable assets, and recovery annotations.
